items.prompt: Assess how far the temperance and Prohibition movements transformed American society between 1890 and 1935.
items.original_prompt: Evaluate the extent to which the Temperance and Prohibition movements transformed American society from 1890 to 1935.

exemplar.thesis: Temperance and Prohibition briefly transformed American law and daily life - achieving a constitutional ban on alcohol - but the experiment's failures, from organized crime to mass noncompliance, showed the limits of legislating morality, ending in repeal.
evidence: The WCTU and Anti-Saloon League built a mass moral-reform movement that won the 18th Amendment (1919)
Prohibition fueled speakeasies, bootlegging, and organized crime (e.g., Capone's Chicago empire), undermining respect for law
The 21st Amendment (1933) repealed Prohibition, marking the only constitutional amendment ever reversed

items.prompt: Assess how far the Massachusetts Bay Colony differed from the Virginia colony between 1607 and 1754.
items.original_prompt: Evaluate the extent to which the Massachusetts Bay Colony differed from the Virginia colony from 1607 to 1754.

exemplar.thesis: Massachusetts Bay and Virginia differed fundamentally in purpose and social order - a Puritan religious refuge built on towns and families versus a profit-driven plantation colony built on bound labor - though both shared an English identity and displaced Native peoples.
evidence: Massachusetts Bay: Puritan mission ('city upon a hill'), town meetings, family farms; Virginia: joint-stock venture, House of Burgesses, tobacco plantations
Labor systems diverged: New England relied on family and town labor while Virginia moved from indentured servitude to enslaved labor
Similarity: both maintained English legal traditions and a strong English identity, and both expanded at Native Americans' expense

items.prompt: Assess how far women's roles in American public life changed between 1920 and 1960.
items.original_prompt: Evaluate the extent to which the roles of women changed in American public life from 1920 to 1960.

exemplar.thesis: Women's public roles expanded dramatically after 1920 through suffrage, wartime work, and new social freedoms, yet the postwar domestic ideal and continued exclusion from political power show how much continuity persisted.
evidence: The 19th Amendment (1920) enfranchised women; flappers and new employment challenged Victorian norms
World War II drew millions of women into factories and services ('Rosie the Riveter')
Continuity: the 1950s suburban domestic ideal, few women in Congress, and persistent wage gaps limited change
